record.one_liner: Chat and community platform with a public REST API and Gateway (WebSocket) for building bots and apps.
record.auth_notes: Bot tokens from the Bot page of the app settings (static, not OAuth) count as api_key; OAuth2 user bearer tokens count as oauth2. OAuth2 token endpoints also accept client_id:client_secret Basic credentials, which is not a username+password so not scored as basic.
record.access_notes: Developer Portal app creation and bot token are self-serve per the bots overview. No paid plan or approval step was seen in the pages fetched; pricing page not checked.
record.api_notes: REST HTTP API plus Gateway for real-time events. No GraphQL seen. Breadth judged from the reference landing page only.
record.blocker_notes: No official Discord MCP server found in vendor pages; a community MCP server (SaseQ, JDA-based) exists. Bot-based use needs no app review in the pages read.

evidence.quote: Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings.
Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the OAuth2 API.
Create an application in the Discord Developer Portal.
Connect to the API using the Gateway for real-time events, the HTTP API for REST operations, or both.
designed to integrate Discord bots with MCP-compatible applications such as Claude
Authenticate as the bot user, not on behalf of any person
